text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Monday:

- Peter Bodenmann told the 'Sonntags-Zeitung' that he will step down from both his job as leader of the Swiss Social Democratic Party and as member of parliament. Bodenmann said he will run for a seat in the cantonal government in his home canton Wallis.
- Jacqueline Maurer of the Swiss Radical Party has been elected as member of the cantonal government in Vaud.

- State-owned telephone company Telecom PTT plans to become negotiable on the stock exchange in the second quarter of 1998. Telecom PTT will become a joint-stock company before the end of the year, according to Felix Rosenberg, chief excecutive of the group.
- Nestle CEO Helmuth Maucher told journalists at the World Economic Forum in Davos that he expected higher growth in both sales and profits for 1997 compared to 1996.

- The Swiss government represented by Flavio Cotti, Kaspar Villiger and Jean-Pascal Delamuraz, speaking on Saturday at the World Economic Forum in Davos, "clarified" the position of Switzerland with regard to the dormant Holocaust accounts.
